$comment: THE CONTRACT LEDGER (Task 043B, R2).
This is the ALLOWLIST of migrations that are permitted to contain contract
operations - drops, renames, type alterations, row rewrites, and raw SQL
this gate cannot read. Everything else inside the compatibility window must
expand only.
It is an allowlist rather than a denylist for the reason the frontend env
allowlist is one: a rule that fires only on operations somebody already
thought of misses the one nobody did. `Sql` is the proof - raw SQL can drop
a table and no operation-name list can see it - so a migration that wants to
be destructive has to SAY SO, here, in a file a reviewer reads.
FIELDS
baseline            the last migration at or before which contract
operations are HISTORY. Read precisely: this is the
grandfather line, not the last deployed migration. A
contract operation in a migration at or before it is
not a finding, because refusing the repository's own
applied past is not a gate, it is a vendetta.
baselineReviewedOn  the date a human last confirmed that line. An
assertion about what is already deployed, with no
date, is never re-examined.
windowReleases      MUST be 1. The frozen rule in
docs/operations/migration-compat.md is one release.
Widening it is a policy change and belongs in that
document, where a reader of the policy will see it.
approvedContracts   one entry per DELIBERATE contract phase. Every field
is required, and each is there because its absence is a
specific failure:
migration    which migration is the contraction
approvedBy   a person or a change-approval record.
An anonymous approval is not an approval.
approvedOn   when. A deletion with no date cannot be
sequenced against the release that made
the data redundant.
reason       why the old shape is safe to remove
NOW, which is a different question from
why it was deprecated.
followUpTask the task that completes the pair. Every
deprecation has one; without it a contract
phase is a deletion whose second half
nobody owns.
reviewBy     when this approval must be revisited.
The task's edge case - a switch left on
forever - has no expiry mechanism other
than a date somebody is accountable for.
An approval past its reviewBy is a finding.
CURRENTLY EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE POINT
No migration in this repository has been through a reviewed contract phase,
so `approvedContracts` is []. The one migration with destructive
operations in its Up - 20260912075115_AddProjectSoftDelete, which drops
outbox_state.bus_name and its index in the same change that adds
dubbing_projects.is_deleted - is at or before the baseline, and that is why
the baseline sits where it does. A new destructive migration fails the gate
with the file and line, and the way out is two releases, not an entry here.
